top news.title: Sources: OpenAI has discussed giving a 5% stake to the US government, seeking to clear political obstacles by securing buy-in from the Trump administration

tweets.author: @thestalwart
tweets.text: I don't know about this path. Rather than equity stakes, why not make companies pay ~20% of all pre-tax income to the federal government? And then instead of exercising shareholder influence, politicians and regulators could set rules on corporate conduct across industries.

tweets.author: @deanwball
tweets.text: There are two broad ways this can work: 1. You divide this 5% over all US households, handing each a direct stake. 2. You give the stake directly to the government. (1) is fine. (2) is probably ruinous, akin to inviting rats to live and reproduce in the walls of your house.

tweets.author: @andrewcurran_
tweets.text: Anthropic is not having any discussions with the White House about a potential government stake. The source in the NOTUS report from a month ago similarly went out of their way to say that the admin was having these kinds of discussions with everyone 𝘦𝘹𝘤𝘦𝘱𝘵 Anthropic. [image]

top news.title: Microsoft invests $2.5B and forms the Microsoft Frontier Company to embed 6,000 forward-deployed engineers with customers to help deploy AI systems

tweets.author: @satyanadella
tweets.text: The future of the firm is a learning loop in which human capital and token capital compound.  With our new Frontier Co., our ambition is to help every enterprise build its own AI capability, and to help create a frontier ecosystem where every organization can turn its knowledge, workflows, and judgment into its own AI systems that continuously improve.

tweets.author: @edzitron
tweets.text: our new management consultancy army will extend the known universe of Microsoft unified support services to leave clients billed with so many different SKUs that they'll need new kinds of math...that's the “Microsoft Way”

tweets.author: @patrickmoorhead
tweets.text: Enterprise AI is hard and getting it wrong or not doing it could end you.  Losing your IP to a frontier model that uses your data and methods to then turn around and compete with you could be the end of a company too.  The middle ground is to have an arbiter, yes that you pay, that has access to all models, frontier to vertical, large to small, harnesses, access to the enterprise data without hijacking it.  The pragmatic part is that huge companies like Microsoft sometimes need focus to speed up and that's what Satya's doing here.  What hasn't been comprehended yet is how to light up the capability where the data sits today which is on-prem.  That's unclear.
